fields.label: Initiative name
fields.help: An initiative is the project or body of work bringing one or more new datasets into EDP. Use the name your team and leadership recognize.

fields.label: Initiative point of contact
fields.help: The person accountable for shepherding this request: you, or someone you name. Being the point of contact does not add anyone to a dataset team or give dataset-owner rights.

fields.label: Data sensitivity
fields.help: Choose the closest classification for the initiative's source data. Some datasets may need extra restrictions; EDP staff will discuss those needs during review.

fields.label: How will your team access this data?
fields.help: Choose how your team expects to query or analyze this data. This does not give other teams access; data permissions are granted separately.

fields.label: Proposed data access approach
fields.placeholder: Describe the tool, application, export, or user workflow you need.
fields.help: Tell EDP who needs the data, which tool or system they use, and what they need to do with it. Leave blank when the approved option already describes the need.

fields.label: Data engineering delivery model
fields.help: Tell EDP who will build and maintain the pipelines. Your own resources may be IRS employees, contractors, or implementation partners.

fields.label: Engineering support needed
fields.placeholder: Describe what your team can build and where you need EDP engineering help.
fields.help: Explain the skills and capacity your team has, the work you need EDP to perform, and any delivery deadline. Leave blank when no additional context is needed.

fields.label: Mission value levers
fields.help: Select every IRS outcome this onboarding advances. The EDP business and ROI review scores the request against these levers.

fields.label: Business justification
fields.placeholder: e.g. Enables the Return Preparer Office to score preparer risk weekly instead of quarterly, closing a tax gap segment and retiring three contractor-run extracts.
fields.help: Include the mission problem, who benefits, the expected outcome, why it is urgent, and the evidence you have.

fields.label: Primary mission outcome
fields.help: Choose the single result that best explains why the initiative matters. You may select several value levers above.

fields.label: Estimated annual benefit (USD)
fields.help: Estimate the annual dollars this work could produce or protect: tax gap reduced through added assessments or collections, fraud or improper payments prevented, direct costs avoided, or another measurable mission result. Enter an amount greater than zero. Explain uncertainty, ranges, and why the work matters in the business justification; EDP staff set mission priority during review.

fields.label: Staff hours saved per year
fields.help: Optional. Include IRS employee, contractor, or operations and maintenance effort avoided.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.help: Only list new data that is not already available in EDP. Check whether it is already available before submitting. Each dataset needs a domain (or a proposed other domain), an ingestion method, a dataset tag, and at least one dataset owner.

fields.label: Must your team's code or work products be hidden from other EDP teams?
options: No — notebooks, code, and dashboard names may be visible in a shared workspace
Yes — code, notebook or dashboard names or contents must be hidden
Not sure — ask EDP staff to assess
fields.help: Most teams use shared workspaces. Data permissions remain separate: sharing a workspace does not give another team access to your data. EDP staff confirm the environment during review. Choose Yes only when the work products themselves must be separated, such as investigative methods.

fields.label: How many people will work on this initiative?
fields.help: Count everyone who will build, test or manage the datasets, not the data consumers who only read them.

fields.label: Workspace separation reason or constraint
fields.placeholder: e.g. investigative methods must not be visible outside the named team, or Not sure what policy applies
fields.help: Optional. Explain any policy, mission, investigation, or other constraint EDP staff should assess. Dedicated-workspace criteria are not automated.

fields.label: Data volume (GB, initial + 1 yr growth)
fields.help: Estimate the total initial data plus one year of growth across this whole initiative, in gigabytes (GB). Leave blank if unknown; EDP staff will refine it.

fields.label: Load frequency
fields.help: How often the initiative expects new or changed source data to arrive. Choose Not sure when the schedule is not established.

fields.label: Transformation complexity
options: Moderate — joins and recurring business rules
Heavy — many joins, large aggregations, or frequent recomputation
Machine learning — feature engineering or model workloads
fields.help: Describe the most demanding transformations across the initiative. Choose the level by the observable examples, or Not sure for EDP staff to assess.

fields.label: Business users needing to query
fields.help: Estimate the total people who will run queries, reports, or dashboards against the initiative's data. This is different from the builders counted on the workspace step.

engModels.name: We have our own resources
engModels.desc: IRS employees, contractors, or implementation partners on our team build and maintain the pipelines using EDP guidance.

engModels.name: Guided build — light platform help
engModels.desc: Our engineers build, with EDP platform team pairing on pattern review, code review and a design walkthrough.

engModels.name: We need data engineering support
engModels.desc: The EDP platform team builds the ingestion and data transformations. EDP staff review whether engineering capacity is available.

ingestPatterns.name: Enterprise File Transfer Utility (EFTU)
ingestPatterns.desc: Scheduled, secure file drops from an IRS source system into EDP.

ingestPatterns.name: Informatica data transfer
ingestPatterns.desc: Informatica extracts data from the source and loads it into EDP for processing.

ingestPatterns.name: Secure cloud storage landing area
ingestPatterns.desc: The source writes files to approved cloud storage and EDP loads them from there.

ingestPatterns.name: I don’t know or need something else — consultation required
ingestPatterns.desc: Choose this when you do not know the transfer path or need something other than EFTU, Informatica, or an EPZ drop. EDP staff will discuss the request with you during review.

accessPatterns.name: All within Databricks
accessPatterns.desc: Notebooks, SQL editor and dashboards inside Databricks only.

accessPatterns.name: Tableau
accessPatterns.desc: Tableau connects to an EDP query service governed by the data catalog.

accessPatterns.name: Power BI
accessPatterns.desc: Power BI connects to an EDP query service governed by the data catalog.

accessPatterns.name: I’m not sure or need another tool — consult EDP staff
accessPatterns.desc: Choose this for extracts to another platform, custom applications, or when you do not know how people will use the data.

source.name: IDRS / Integrated Data Retrieval System
source.desc: Account and case data from the IDRS operational system.

source.name: Other / not listed (needs consultation)
source.desc: A source system not in the approved catalog requires an EDP data architecture consultation.

roiLevers.name: Reduce fraud and improper payments
roiLevers.measure: Estimate refund fraud / improper payments prevented per year.

roiLevers.name: Reduce the tax gap
roiLevers.measure: Estimate additional assessments or collections enabled per year.

roiLevers.name: Better taxpayer services
roiLevers.measure: Estimate value of faster case resolution and fewer taxpayer touches.

roiLevers.name: Reduce cost and contractor support
roiLevers.measure: Estimate contractor hours and O&M dollars avoided per year.

roiLevers.name: Reduce IT spend / retire duplicate systems
roiLevers.measure: Estimate license, hosting and duplicate-system costs retired per year.

roiLevers.name: Improve data quality, security and compliance posture
roiLevers.measure: Estimate rework, audit findings and manual controls avoided per year.

computePolicy.title: Standard compute policy
computePolicy.summary: Every initiative starts on EDP's standard compute policy. This is an overview only — there is nothing to choose here.

items.label: All-purpose compute
items.value: Standard access mode (user isolation) under the all-purpose cluster policy

items.label: Job compute
items.value: Job clusters under the job cluster policy, ending when each run finishes

items.label: SQL warehouse
items.value: A SQL warehouse in every environment, created at standup

items.label: Other limits
items.value: Runtime, autoscaling and cost ceilings aren't set by the policy yet

computePolicy.changeNote: Need something different? You can ask EDP to change your compute policy after your initiative is active.
